{{Citation needed|date=November 2019|qq=}}
'''Awashi''' (阿波志) is a {{ill|Chorography|en|Chorography|qid=Q2088593|lt=topographical record}} of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|qid=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)}} (modern-day {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|qid=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture}}), compiled during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} by the {{ill|Tokushima Domain|en|Tokushima Domain|qid=Q3034557|lt=Tokushima Domain}}.<ref name="Britannica-Awashi"/><ref name="Yamakawa-HistoryDictionary"/><ref name="TokushimaMuseum-20190207"/>
== Compilation History ==
The 11th lord of the Tokushima Domain, {{ill|Hachisuka Haruaki|en|Hachisuka Haruaki|qid=Q3125457|lt=Hachisuka Haruaki}}, appointed the Confucian scholar Sano Yamakage (also known as Sano Yukinori<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/> or Fujihara Yukinori<ref name="Nihonjinmei-Daijiten-SanoYamakage"/>; 1751–1819<ref name="Nihonjinmei-Daijiten-SanoYamakage"/>) in {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei}} 4 (1792) to oversee the compilation of "Awashi."<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/><ref name="KawadeHistoryDictionary"/>
In {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei}} 5 (1793), Sano ordered geographical surveys of towns, villages, and ports within the domain.<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/><ref name="Britannica-Awashi"/> Information was collected through local officials and village headmen, covering geography, history, population, agricultural yields, and shrines and temples.<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/><ref name="Nipponica-Awashi"/> In {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei}} 10 (1798), Sano conducted his own inspections, collecting additional data.<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/>
The compilation was completed in {{ill|Culture|en|Culture|qid=Q11042|lt=Bunka}} 12 (1815), 23 years after its initiation, as a 12-volume work titled "Awashi."<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/><ref name="KawadeHistoryDictionary"/><ref name="Yamakawa-HistoryDictionary"/><ref name="Britannica-Awashi"/><ref name="Nipponica-Awashi"/> Despite its Completion tier 3]]
, its content is concise without referencing primary historical documents.<ref name="PrefecturalMuseum"/>
The 12 volumes are structured as follows:<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/>
* Volume 1 - Overview of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|en|Awa Province (Tokushima)|qid=Q907457|lt=Awa Province (Tokushima)}}
* Volume 2 - {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|qid=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle}} and its surroundings
* Volume 3 - {{ill|Itano District, Tokushima|en|Itano District, Tokushima|qid=Q1156025|lt=Itano District}}
* Volume 4 - {{ill|Awa District, Tokushima|en|Awa District, Tokushima|qid=Q4829634|lt=Awa District, Tokushima}}
* Volume 5 - {{ill|Mima District, Tokushima|en|Mima District, Tokushima|qid=Q1156496|lt=Mima District, Tokushima}}
* Volume 6 - {{ill|Miyoshi District, Tokushima|en|Miyoshi District, Tokushima|qid=Q1156031|lt=Miyoshi District, Tokushima}}
* Volume 7 - {{ill|Oe District, Tokushima|en|Oe District, Tokushima|qid=Q3205811|lt=Oe District, Tokushima}}
* Volume 8 - {{ill|Myōdō District, Tokushima|en|Myōdō District, Tokushima|qid=Q1156486|lt=Myōdō District, Tokushima}}
* Volume 9 - {{ill|Myōzai District, Tokushima|en|Myōzai District, Tokushima|qid=Q1155732|lt=Nishi District, Tokushima}}
* Volume 10 - {{ill|Katsuura District, Tokushima|en|Katsuura District, Tokushima|qid=Q1119478|lt=Katsura District, Tokushima}}
* Volume 11 - {{ill|Naka District, Tokushima|en|Naka District, Tokushima|qid=Q1156492|lt=Naka District, Tokushima}}
* Volume 12 - {{ill|Kaifu District|ja|海部郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaifu District, Tokushima|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11151382}}
== Existing Copies ==
; Gotō Family Copy (Hachisuka Library)
Held by the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀家|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachisuka family|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 蜂須賀氏|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2975261}}, this version is stamped with the "Hachisuka Library" seal.<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/> Designated as a tangible cultural property of Tokushima Prefecture and preserved at the {{ill|Tokushima Castle Museum|ja|徳島城博物館|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Castle Museum|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳島市立徳島城博物館|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11489793}}.<ref name="PrefecturalMuseum"/>
; Kurego Library Copy (Awa Province Library)
A transcription made in {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 31 (1898), followed by another transcription in {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 45 (1912). This version bears the "Awa Province Library" seal.<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/> Preserved at the {{ill|National Diet Library|en|National Diet Library|qid=Q477675|lt=National Diet Library}}.<ref name="PrefecturalMuseum"/>{{refnest|group="note"|As of 2000, listed under the Tokushima Prefectural Library's collection.<ref name="Heibonsha-Awashi"/>|qq=}}
; Printed Version
In {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 6 (1931), a printed version by Kasai Aisui was released, with a reprint in 1976.<ref name="NII-Awashi-1976"/> The printed edition contains errors and structural differences from the original.<ref name="PrefecturalMuseum"/>
== Evaluation ==
The compilation of "Awashi" coincided with financial struggles within the Tokushima Domain. It is believed that the domain intended to utilize the record for agricultural and administrative reform.<ref name="Nipponica-Awashi"/>

== Alternative Version: ''Ihon Awa-shi'' ==
An alternative gazetteer titled ''Awa-shi,'' of unknown authorship and compilation date, exists. To distinguish it from the Tokushima Domain's ''Awa-shi,'' it is referred to as ''Ihon Awa-shi'' (Alternative ''Awa-shi''). It provides richer content, including significant insights into the founding of Tokushima Castle Town. Numerous manuscript copies suggest its high regard.<ref name="Heibon-Geography-Awash"/>
The compilation date varies by account, with some sources suggesting {{ill|1757|en|1757|qid=Q7635|lt=1757}} (7th year of [[:en:Horeki|Horeki]]) or {{ill|1763|en|1763|qid=Q7655|lt=1763}} (13th year of Horeki). However, the text also includes details from the {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei}} era (1789–1801), leading to theories that it was completed during this period or between the Horeki and {{ill|Meiwa|en|Meiwa|qid=Q1146161|lt=Meiwa}} (1764–1772) eras.<ref name="Heibon-Geography-Awash"/>
